sections.body: The AI Accountant covers ten areas where artificial intelligence is changing accounting and finance. In practice, AI is used to read invoices, match payments, draft journal entries, reconcile accounts, flag unusual transactions, and produce first drafts of reports. It also supports forecasting by finding patterns in historical data, tax work by classifying transactions across jurisdictions, and audit by testing full populations instead of samples. The work is not fully autonomous. People still set accounting policy, approve judgments, and sign off on filings. The field sits between software that automates routine steps and systems that assist professional judgment.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are mature, and payables and receivables automation, bank reconciliation, and anomaly detection are widely deployed and often work well on clean, high volume data. Forecasting and planning tools can improve speed and scenario coverage, but they depend on data quality and still need human review. Tax and jurisdictional compliance remains difficult because rules change and vary by location. Continuous audit and assurance is promising but not a replacement for professional judgment or regulatory inspection. Fraud detection finds patterns but also produces false positives and can miss novel schemes. Governance, risk and financial data security are unresolved in many organizations, and the site tracks 222 compliance and regulation pages, which shows how much rule making surrounds the work.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section follow the money and the controls around it. Financial Reporting and Synthesis covers the close and the production of statements, while Forecasting and Planning covers budgets, scenarios, and driver based models. Tax and Jurisdictional Compliance deals with filings and cross border rules, and Continuous Audit and Assurance deals with monitoring and testing. Fraud Detection and Forensics looks at misuse and investigation, while Payables and Receivables and Treasury and Liquidity cover cash movement, working capital, and funding. Sustainability and Carbon Accounting and Digital Asset Accounting cover newer reporting areas with their own measurement problems. Governance, Risk and Financial Data Security ties the set together by asking who owns the model, how data is protected, and how errors are caught.
